name: Scoresheet
intent: Rate the same thing at the start and the end so the change is visible.
when: confidence, mood, or commitment likely to shift across the sitting

variants.label: Mark a track as the session goes
variants.prompt: Mark the next cell on each track whenever the tracked thing moves, or mark done, partial, or missed each time if you're using three states.
variants.readback: Read the shape the marks make across the track, not the count of marks; a gap in the middle is more informative than the total.

variants.label: Rate each life domain; compare across returns
variants.prompt: Rate each life domain today, write one line on why, then copy last time's rating in from the previous page.
variants.readback: The domain that moved most since last time is this page's real output; a domain that never moves is worth its own line too.

claims.claim: People recall their earlier attitudes, feelings or confidence as closer to their present state than they were, or as fitting their theory of how they must have changed. A written baseline is therefore needed to see real change.
claims.construct: consistency and change biases in autobiographical memory (implicit theories of stability and change)

claims.claim: Monitoring progress towards a goal increases goal attainment, and more so when the progress is physically recorded.
Rating satisfaction in several named life domains gives a reliable and valid measure of subjective well-being, and it shows which domain drives a change that a single overall rating hides.
claims.construct: domain satisfaction; the Personal Wellbeing Index; bottom-up models of life satisfaction

sources.cite: International Wellbeing Group (2013), Personal Wellbeing Index manual

grounding.helps: when you want to see which part of life moved between returns: rating named domains follows an established well-being measure whose answers are stable over weeks and change little with rating order; the page measures, it does not improve anything
grounding.backfires: when the domains change from one return to the next, when an average is allowed to hide the one domain that matters, or when the ratings are read as a score to raise

prompt: Rate each line now; rate it again at the end. The change matters more than the number.
readback: Compare start and end ratings; a large move on one line is the session's real output.

claims.claim: People recall their earlier attitudes, feelings or confidence as closer to their present state than they were, or as fitting their theory of how they must have changed. A written baseline is therefore needed to see real change.
claims.construct: consistency and change biases in autobiographical memory (implicit theories of stability and change)

claims.claim: Monitoring progress towards a goal increases goal attainment, and more so when the progress is physically recorded.

grounding.helps: when a felt sense is likely to shift: writing the before rating down means the after rating is compared with what you actually said, not with a memory that drifts towards how you feel now
grounding.backfires: when the numbers become a target, since rewards tied to a monitored target undermine interest in the activity, and when the visible before rating anchors the after one; whether hiding it helps is untested
